findings.title: Warning skips IPsec, which also adds encryption overhead
findings.explanation: The doc comment says the function warns about any feature that adds encapsulation or encryption overhead, and NewConfiguration (just above the call site) does reduce the route MTU for IPsec using p.IPsec.Enabled() and AuthKeySize. The check here only looks at WireGuard and tunnelling. So a chained setup that uses IPsec in native-routing mode, with route MTU not managed, gets no warning, even though it has the same fragmentation risk this change is meant to flag.
findings.suggestion: Add the IPsec case: `if p.WgConfig.Enabled() || p.IPsec.Enabled() || p.TunnelConfig.ShouldAdaptMTU() {`

findings.title: Empty chaining mode is not treated as 'no chaining'
findings.explanation: The early return only matches the exact string "none". If the CNI config manager reports an unset chaining mode as "" (the flag default or an omitted Helm value), every non-chained cluster running in tunnel mode (the default) or with WireGuard would log this fragmentation warning on startup. That is a misleading warning on a common path. Whether this happens depends on how cni-chaining-mode defaults are normalised, which isn't visible in this file.
findings.suggestion: Treat both values as 'no chaining': `if m := p.CNI.GetChainingMode(); m == "" || m == "none" || cc.EnableRouteMTUForCNIChaining { return }`
